वनिन: वनिन, अम्, n., Ved. anything growing in a forest, a tree.
वनिल: वनिल, see Gaṇa Kāśādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80.
वनिष्ठ: वनिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. obtaining most; bestowing or imparting most, very munificent or liberal, (Sāy. = दातृतम।)
वनिष्ठु: वनिष्ठु, उस्, m., Ved. part of the entrails of an animal offered in sacrifice; the rectum; (according to others) a part of the intestines near the omentum, (Sāy. = स्थविरान्त्र।)
वनी: वनी, f. See under 1. वन, p. 883, col. 2.
वनीक: वनीक or वनीपक or वनीयक, अस्, m. a beggar, mendicant.
वनीय: वनीय, Nom. P. वनीयति, &c., to beg, ask alms; to entreat, request.
वनीयस्: वनीयस्, आन्, असी, अस्, asking or obtaining more, obtaining most; to be honoured, to be favoured, (Sāy. = सम्भजनीय = सम्भाव्य); imparting or bestowing most.
वनीवन्: वनीवन्, आ, आ, अ (an Intensive form), asking for, demanding, (Sāy. = वनन-वत्।)
वनु: वनु, उस्, m., Ved. one who plots against or injures, a malignant or malicious person, (Sāy. = हिंसक); an adherent (?).
वनुष: वनुष (fr. वनुस्), Nom. A. वनुषते, &c., Ved. to obtain, acquire; (Sāy.) to worship.
वनुष्य: वनुष्य (fr. वनुस्), Nom. P. A. वनुष्यति, -ते, &c., Ved. to have a design upon, plot against, seek to injure, to be fond of battle; to emulate (with inst.); to overpower, defeat, attack, (according to Naigh. II. 12 = क्रुध्यति; according to Nirukta V. 2 = हन्ति); (A.) to wish for, desire, (Sāy. on Ṛg-veda IX. 7, 6. वनुष्यते = सेव्यते।)
वनुष्यत्: वनुष्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, seeking to injure, ma-levolent, hostile, an enemy.
वनुस्: वनुस्, उस्, उस्, उस्, Ved. desiring, anxious for, eager, zealous; devoted, attached to, loving; enjoying, an enjoyer, worshipping, a worshipper, honourer, (Sāy. = सम्भक्तृ); (उस्), m. any one eager to injure (others), an enemy, plotter, warrior; the act of possess-ing, enjoying, distributing, (Sāy. = सम्भजन।)
वनेज्य: वनेज्य, अस्, m. a kind of mango.
वनेयु: वनेयु, उस्, m., N. of a son of Raudrāśva.
वन्ति: वन्ति, इस्, f., see Pāṇ. VI. 4, 39.
वन्तृ: वन्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who enjoys or possesses, a possessor, owner, (Sāy. = सम्भक्तृ।)
वन्य: वन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, growing in woods, of or be-longing to a wood, forest, produced in a wood, living in woods, wild, savage; being or existing in a wood (said of Agni, Ved.); made of wood, wooden; (अस्), m. an animal of the forest, wild animal, wild beast; a wild plant; N. of particular wild plants (= वन-शूरण, वाराही-कन्द, देव-नाल); (आ), f. a multitude of groves, a large forest; abundance of water, a flood, deluge; N. of various plants, Physalis Flexuosa; = मद्गु-पर्णी, गोपाल-कर्कटी, गुञ्जा, मिश्रेया, भद्र-मुस्ता, गन्ध-पत्त्रा; (अम्), n. anything grown in a wood, the fruit or roots of wild plants; = त्वच; [cf. other meanings of the word वन्य in चक्षुर्-व्°, अजीत-पुनर्वण्य।] —वन्य-द्विप, अस्, m. a wild elephant. —वन्य-पक्षिन्, ई, m. a wild bird, forest bird; [cf. पुर-पक्षिन्।] —वन्य-वृत्ति, इस्, f. forest fare. —व-न्याशन (°य-अश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, eating wild fruits, &c. —वन्येतर (°य-इत्°), अस्, आ, अत्, different from wild tame, civilized.
वन्योपादकी: वन्योपादकी, f. a kind of creeper.
ववन्वस्: ववन्वस्, वान्, उषी, वत्, Ved. one who has desired or asked.
वनर्गु: वनर्गु वनर्-गु। See under वनस्, p. 884.
वनहबन्दि: वनहबन्दि वनहबन्दि, N. of a place.
वनाहिर: वनाहिर वनाहिर, अस्, m. a hog, wild boar.
वनीवाहन: वनीवाहन वनीवाहन, अम्, n. (an anoma-lous Intens. fr. rt. 1. वह्), Ved. the act of carrying or moving hither and thither.
वनौकस्: वनौकस् वनौकस्, वनौषधि। See p. 884, cols. 2, 3.
वन्तव: वन्तव वन्तव (?) , अस्, m. a proper N.
वन्द्: वन्द् वन्द् (connected with rt. वद्), cl. 1. A. (Ved. and ep. sometimes P.) वन्-दते, ववन्दे (Ved. ववन्द, ववन्दिम), अवन्-दिष्ट, वन्दितुम् (Ved. Inf. वन्दध्यै), to praise, celebrate, laud, extol, eulogize, bless, pro-nounce a blessing; to show honour, do homage, salute respectfully, greet, make obeisance to; to venerate, worship, adore: Pass. वन्द्यते, Aor. अवन्दि, to be praised, &c.: Caus. वन्दयति, -यते, -यितुम्, Aor. अववन्दत्, अववन्दत, to show honour to any one, make obeisance to, greet respect-fully.
वन्द: वन्द, अस्, आ, अम्, praising, extolling; [cf. देव-वन्द।]
वन्दक: वन्दक, अस्, आ, m. f. a praiser, &c.; a parasitical plant.
वन्दथ: वन्दथ, अस्, m. a praiser, panegyrist, eulogist, bard; one deserving praise.
वन्दद्वार: वन्दद्-वार, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. blessing the mul-titude, i. e. men, (in Sāma-veda I. 1, 2, 3, 6. for वन्दे दारुम्, which is the correct reading in the corresponding passage of the Ṛg-veda.)
वन्दद्वीर: वन्दद्-वीर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. blessing heroes, (in Sāma-veda I. 4, 2, 3, 1. for मन्दद्-वीर, which is the correct reading in the corresponding passage of the Ṛg-veda.)
वन्दन: वन्दन, अस्, m., N. of a Ṛṣi (described in Ṛg-veda I. 112, 5. as having been cast into a well, along with Rebha, by the Asuras, and rescued by the Aśvins); (आ), f. praise, praising, worship, adoration; a mark or sign worn on the body (made with ashes &c.); (ई), f. making obeisance, reverence, worship, adoring; begging, soliciting, asking; the hip (?) ; a drug for reviving the dead; (अम्), n. the act of praising, praise; obeisance to a Brāhman or superior (by touching the feet &c.), reverence, adoration; the face, mouth (= वदन); a parasitical plant (perhaps a kind of lichen); a disease attacking the limbs or joints, a cutaneous eruption, scrofula (some-times personified as a demon). —वन्दन-माला or वन्दन-मालिका, f. a festoon suspended across gate-ways (in honour of the arrival of any distinguished personage, or on the occasion of a marriage or other festival). —वन्दन-श्रुत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. listening to praise, a hearer of praises, (Sāy. = स्तुतीनां श्रोतृ।)
वन्दनीय: वन्दनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be praised or wor-shipped, praiseworthy, adorable, to be greeted with homage, to be saluted or made obeisance to; (अस्), m. a yellow-flowering Verbesina; (आ), f. the yellow pigment called गो-रोचना, q. v.
वन्दमान: वन्दमान, अस्, आ, अम्, praising, celebrating, pro-nouncing a blessing, honouring, reverencing.
वन्दयित्वा: वन्दयित्वा, ind. (fr. the Caus.), having praised, having saluted or shown honour to, having made obeisance to.
वन्दा: वन्दा, f. a parasitical plant, the parasitical plant Epidendrum Tesselatum, &c.; a female beggar or mendicant; = वन्दि, वन्दी।
वन्दाक: वन्दाक, अस्, m., आ, ई, f. a parasitical plant.
वन्दार: वन्दार, अस्, m. a parasitical plant.
वन्दारु: वन्दारु, उस्, उस्, उ, praising, celebrating; respect-ful, reverential, civil, complimentary, polite; (उस्), m. a panegyrist, bard; a proper N.; (उ), n. praise.
वन्दि: 1. वन्दि, इस्, m. (for 2. वन्दि see col. 3), a praiser, panegyrist, &c. (= वन्दिन्).

वन्दि 2. वन्दि, इस्, or वन्दी, f. (more pro-perly written बन्दि, बन्दी; probably connected with rt. बन्ध्, cf. the Persian بنده for 1. वन्दि see col. 2), a captive or prisoner in general (male or female); a woman in captivity, female captive or slave; an animal confined in a cage; a ladder or stairs; plunder, booty, spoil. —वन्दि-ग्राह, अस्, m. ‘plunder-seizer,’ a housebreaker (especially one breaking into a temple or place where sacred fire is preserved). —वन्दि-चौर, अस्, m. = वन्दि-ग्राह above. —वन्दी-कार, अस्, m. one who commits robbery, a robber, thief, housebreaker, bur-glar. —वन्दी-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्तुम्, to make captive, take prisoner, capture, rob. —वन्दी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made prisoner, taken captive. —वन्दी-पाल, अस्, m. a keeper of prisoners, a jailor.
वन्दित: वन्दित, अस्, आ, अम्, praised, extolled, celebrated.
वन्दितव्य: वन्दितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be praised or cele-brated, laudable, to be treated with awe or respect, one to whom obeisance is to be made.
वन्दितृ: वन्दितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. one who praises or celebrates, a praiser.
वन्दिन्: वन्दिन्, ई, m. one who praises or extols, a praiser, panegyrist, encomiast, bard, poet, herald (whose duty is to proclaim the titles of a great man as he passes along, or who sings the praises of a prince in his presence or accompanies an army to chaunt martial songs; these bards are regarded as belonging to a distinct tribe, being considered the descendants of a Kṣatriya by a Śūdra female); a captive, slave, (in this sense more properly written बन्दिन्, cf. 2. वन्दि।) —वन्दि-पाठ, अस्, m. the panegyric of a bard or Vandin, eulogium.
वन्दिनीका: वन्दिनीका or वन्दिनीया, f., N. of Dākṣāyaṇī.
वन्द्य: वन्द्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be praised, laudable, com-mendable, praiseworthy; to be reverentially saluted, to be honoured or worshipped, adorable, very vene-rable; to be regarded or respected; (अस्), m. a proper N.; (आ), f. = वन्दा, a parasitical plant; = गो-रोचना; N. of a Yakṣī. —वन्द्य-ता, f. lauda-bility, praiseworthiness, venerableness.
वन्द्यमान: वन्द्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being praised or cele-brated, being saluted or greeted.
वन्द्र: वन्द्र, अस्, आ, अम्, praising, worshipping, honour-ing, doing homage; (अस्), m. a worshipper, votary, follower; (अम्), n. prosperity.
वन्दीक: वन्दीक वन्दीक, अस्, m. (also written बन्-दीक), N. of Indra.
वन्धा: वन्धा वन्धा, ind., see Gaṇa Ūry-ādi to Pāṇ. I. 4, 61.
वन्धुर्: वन्धुर्, m., Ved. = वन्धुर above; (in Atharva-veda III. 9, 3. the sense is doubtful.)
वन्धुर: वन्धुर वन्धुर, अम्, n. (probably con-nected with rt. बन्ध् and perhaps more properly written बन्धुर), the seat of a charioteer, the fore part of a chariot or place at the end of the shafts, a carriage-seat or driver's box; the frame-work [cf. हिरण्य-व्°] of a carriage, (the word वन्-धुरम् occurs frequently in Ved. and is variously explained by Sāy. as नीड-बन्धनाधार-भूतम्, उन्नतानत-रूप-बन्धन-काष्ठम्, वेष्टि-तं सारथेः स्थानम्, सारथ्य्-आश्रय-स्थानम्, &c.; the car of the Aśvins, which is described as ‘three-wheeled’ as well as triple in other parts of its construction, is said to be also त्रि-वन्धुर or त्रि-बन्धुर, i. e. ‘having three poles or pieces of wood for securing the occupant’ or ‘having a triple standing-place or seat for the charioteer.’) —वन्धुरे-ष्ठा, आस्, आस्, अम् (i. e. वन्धुरे, loc. c. + स्था), Ved. standing or sitting on the chariot-seat.
वन्धुरायु: वन्धुरायु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. having a standing-place in front or a seat for driving (said of the car of the Aśvins).
वन्धुल: वन्धुल वन्धुल, अस्, m. (also written बन्-धुल, q. v.), N. of a Ṛṣi.
वन्ना: वन्ना वन्ना, f., N. of a woman.
वन्र: वन्र वन्र, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. II. 28. fr. rt. 1. वन्), a co-partner, co-heir.
वप्: वप् वप्, cl. 1. P. A. वपति, वपते, उवाप (1st sing. उवप or उवाप, 2nd sing. उवपिथ), ऊपे (according to some also [आ]वेपे), वप्स्यति, -ते (ep. वपिष्यति), अवाप्सीत्, अवप्त, वप्तुम्, to shear, cut, shave (the hair, beard, &c., Ved.); to shear off, crop off, eat off, graze, mow (grass &c., in Ṛg-veda VI. 6, 4. वपन्ति = मुण्-डयन्ति); to shave one's self, be shaven or shorn (Ved. A.); to strew, scatter (especially seed), sow seed, sow, plant; to throw, cast (dice &c.); to pro-create, beget; to weave, (in this sense probably a kind of Caus. of rt. वे): Pass. उप्यते (Part. उप्त, q. v.; the forms उपित and वपित are also given), to be scattered or sown: Caus. वापयति, -यते, -यितुम्, Aor. अवीवपत्, to cause to shear or shave (Ved.); to cause to be shorn (Ved. A.); to sow, put in the ground, plant: Desid. विवप्सति, -ते: Intens. वावप्यते, वावप्ति; [cf. Gr. ὀπυίω, οἴφω, οἰφέω, (perhaps also) ὅπλοω, ὑφαίνω; Angl. Sax. wif, wœpen; Goth. vepn.]
वप: वप, अस्, m. shaving, shearing; one who sows, a sower; sowing seed; weaving; (आ), f. the skin or covering of the intestines, omentum; the mucous or glutinous secretion of the bones or flesh, marrow, fat (= मेदस्, q. v.); a mound or heap thrown up by ants; a cavity, hollow, hole. —वपा-कृत्, त्, m. marrow. —वपा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, furnished with omentum, enveloped in omentum, covered with fat, &c. —वपोदर (°पा-उद्°), अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. fat-bellied, corpulent (said of Indra).
वपन: वपन, अम्, n. the act of shearing, shaving; the act of sowing seed, sowing; semen virile; (ई), f. a barber's shop.
वपनीय: वपनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be shorn [cf. केश-व्°]; to be sown.
वपिल: वपिल, अस्, m. a procreator, father.
वपु: वपु, उस्, m. a body; (उस्), f., N. of an Apsaras.
वपुन: वपुन, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. वप्), a deity; (अम्), n. knowledge, (probably for वयुन।)
वपुष: वपुष, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. = वपुस्, having form or beautiful form, handsome, (according to modern Vedic scholars also) wonderful; (अम्), n. beauty or elegance of form, wonderful figure, (Sāy. on Ṛg-veda III. 2, 15. वपुषाय = रूपार्थम्, for beauty of form, on account of beauty of form); body, form, (at the end of a comp., cf. वराह-व्°); (आ), f. a particular article of commerce (= हवुषा?).
वपुष्य: 1. वपुष्य, Nom. P. वपुष्यति, &c., Ved. to cause beauty or lustre of form, (Sāy. वपुर्-दीप्तिं कृ); to desire form or beauty of form, (Sāy. = वपुर् इष्); to wonder, be astonished, (this latter sense is thought probable by modern scholars.)
2. वपुष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having form or beauty of form, handsome; conducive to bodily welfare, (Sāy. = वपुषि हित); wonderfully beauti-ful, wonderful.
वपुस्: वपुस्, उस्, उस्, उस्, having form or beautiful form (Ved.), embodied, handsome, (according to modern Vedic scholars also) wonderful; (उस्), n. form, figure, shape, body, person, appearance; essence, nature, character; a beautiful form or figure; beautiful ap-pearance, beauty, (वपुषे, dat. c. for beauty of form, in order to be beautiful); beautiful or won-derful appearance of any kind, (according to modern Vedic scholars) marvellous phenomenon, wonder; water (according to Naigh. I. 12); N. of a daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Dharma. —वपुः-प्रकर्-ष, अस्, m. excellence of form, personal beauty. —वपुः-स्रव, अस्, m. a humor of the body. —वपुर्-धर, अस्, आ, अम्, having form, em-bodied, having beautiful form, beautiful, handsome. —वपुष्-टम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. most beautiful or excellent in form, most beautiful or handsome; most wonderful; (आ), f. Hibiscus Mutabilis; N. of the wife of Janam-ejaya. —वपुष्-टर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. more or most beautiful in form, more handsome, more or most wonderful. —व-पुष्-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a body, corpo-real, corporate, embodied; having a beautiful form, beautiful, handsome; containing the word वपुस्; (आन्), m., N. of a deity enumerated among the Viśve Devāḥ; of a son of Priya-vrata; of a king of Kuṇḍina; (अती), f., N. of one of the Mātṛs attending upon Skanda. —वपुष्-मत, अस्, m., N. of a king of Kuṇḍina, (for वपुष्-मत्।) —वपुस्-सात्, ind. into the state of a body, to a form or body.
वप्तव्य: वप्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be sown; to be immitted seminally; to be impregnated or begotten; to be implanted, to be given or conferred.
वप्तृ: वप्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who shears, a shearer, cutter, shaver; one who sows or plants, a planter, sower, husbandman; (ता), m. one who fertilizes or fecundates, a procreator, progenitor, father; a poet, sage.
वप्र: वप्र, अस्, अम्, m. n. a rampart, earth-work, mud-wall, mound, hillock, earth taken from the ditch of a town and raised as a wall or buttress; the foundation of a building; the gate of a fortified city; the bank of a river, shore or bank in general, (अनु-वप्रम्, along the bank or shore, Kirāt. VI. 4); the slope or declivity of a hill, table-land on a mountain; a ditch; the circumference of a sphere or globe; a sown field, field in general; dust, earth; the butting of an elephant or bull, (see वप्र-क्रीडा); = निष्-कुट, वन-ज, वाजिका (?), पाटीर; (अम्), n. lead [cf. वर्ध्र]; (अस्), m. a father [cf. वप्तृ]; = प्रजा-पति; N. of a Vyāsa in the fourteenth division of the Dvāpara age; of a son of the fourteenth Manu; (आ), f. Bengal madder (= मञ्जिष्ठा); N. of the mother of Nimi (the twenty-first Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī); (ई), f. a hillock, ant-hill. —वप्र-क्रिया, f. = वप्र-क्रीडा below. —वप्र-क्रीडा, f. the playful butting (of an elephant or bull) against a bank or mound of any kind, (this is called तटाघात in Kumāra-s. II. 50.) —वप्रानत (°र-आन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, bowed or stooping to butt at a bank or wall. —वप्रान्तर् (°र-अन्°), ind. in or between banks or mounds. —वप्राभिघात (°र-अभ्°), अस्, m. butting at a bank or mound. —वप्राम्भः-स्रुति, इस्, f. the stream of water flowing along a bank or issuing from a bank, a rivulet. —वप्राम्भस् (°र-अम्°), अस्, n. the water flowing along a bank.
वप्रक: वप्रक, अस्, m. the circumference of a sphere.
वप्रि: वप्रि = क्षेत्र, a field; = दुर्-गति, समुद्र।
वप्सस्: वप्सस्, Ved. form, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 181, 8 = वपुस् or रूप।)

Varuṇa is one of the oldest of the Vedic gods, corresponding in name and partly in character to the Οὐρανός of the Greeks, and is often regarded as the supreme deity, being then styled ‘king of the gods’ or ‘king of both gods and men’ or ‘king of the universe;’ no other deity has such grand attributes and functions assigned to him; he is described as fashioning and upholding heaven and earth, as possessing extraordinary power and wisdom called माया, as sending his spies or messen-gers throughout both worlds, as numbering the very winkings of men's eyes, as hating falsehood, as seizing transgressors with his पाश or noose, as in-flicting diseases, especially dropsy, as pardoning sin, as the guardian of immortality; though generally associated with Mitra, he is also invoked in the Veda together with Indra, and in later Vedic literature together with Agni, with Yama, and with Viṣṇu; in Ṛg-veda IV. 1, 2. he is even called the brother of Agni; though not generally regarded in the Veda as a god of the ocean, yet he is often connected with the waters, especially the waters of the atmosphere or firmament, and in one place [Ṛg-veda VII. 64, 2] is called with Mitra सिन्धु-पति, ‘lord of the sea or of rivers;’ hence in the later mythology he became a kind of Neptune, and is there best known in his character of god of the ocean; in the Mahā-bhārata Varuṇa is said to be a son of Kardama and father of Puṣkara, and is also variously represented as one of the Deva-gandharvas, as a Nāga, as a king of the Nāgas, and as an Asura; he is the regent of the western quarter [cf. लोक-पाल] and of the Nakṣatra Śata-bhiṣaj; the Jainas consider Varuṇa as a servant of the twentieth Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī); the sun (‘the warder off or dispeller of darkness,’ cf. (per-haps) the gods generally (so explained by some in Atharva-veda III. 4, 6); (आ), f., N. of a river; [cf. Zend Varena; Gr.
