वेत्रिन्: वेत्रिन्, ई, m. a staff-bearer, mace-bearer, porter, door-keeper.
वेथ्: वेथ् वेथ् (= rts. विथ्, 1. विध्), cl. 1. A. वेथते, विवेथे, वेथिष्यते, अवेथिष्ट, वेथितुम्, to ask, beg.
वेथिलेह: वेथिलेह वेथिलेह, N. of a place.
वेदन: वेदन, अम्, आ, n. f. perception, knowledge; knowledge obtained by the senses, feeling, sensation; obtaining, acquisition, property, wealth; presenting, delivering; marrying, marriage; the marriage of a Śūdra woman with a man of a higher caste, (see Manu III. 44; cf. उत्कृष्ट-व्°); the ceremony of holding the ends of a mantle (observed by a Śūdra female on her marriage with a man of a higher caste); (ई), f. the true skin or cutis; (आ), f. pain, torment, smart, agony; Pain or Torture (per-sonified as a daughter of An-ṛta). —वेदना-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessed of pain, full of aches.
वेदनीय: वेदनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be perceived, perceptible; capable of being felt; to be known or understood; to be made known.
वेदय: 1. वेदय, अस्, आ, अम्, who or what knows, know-ing; who or what obtains.
वेदयान: वेदयान, अस्, आ, अम्, causing to know, making known, telling, (अ-वेदयान, not informing.)
वेदस्: वेदस्, आस्, m. the Vedas collectively; (अस्), n. acquisition, wealth (Ved.).
वेदस्; under अस्, n. add — knowledge; (वेदास्, nom. m. although given by some authorities is pro-bably only nom. pl. of वेद।)
वेदापय: वेदापय, Nom. P. वेदापयति, -यितुम्, to cause to know, impart knowledge.
वेदि: वेदि, इस्, or वेदी, f. (in Śatapatha-Brāhmaṇa I. 2, 5, 7. said to be fr. rt. 1. विद्, ‘to acquire;’ but per-haps connected with rt. वे, ‘to weave or bind to-gether’), an altar or raised place made of Kuśa grass or strewed with it and prepared for an oblation for placing the vessels used at a sacrifice, a place or ground prepared for sacrifice, (it is more or less raised and of various shapes); an altar (in general); a quadrangular spot in the court-yard of a temple or palace (usually furnished with a raised floor or seat and covered with a roof supported by pillars, = वि-तर्दि); a bench; a seal-ring; N. of Sarasvatī (wife of Brahmā); (इस्), m. a teacher, Paṇḍit. —वेदि-जा, f. ‘altar-born,’ epithet of Draupadī, wife of the Pāṇḍu princes, (the fee which Droṇa required for instructing the Pāṇḍu princes was that they should conquer Drupada, king of Pañcāla, who had insulted him; they therefore took him prisoner, and he, burning with resentment, undertook a sacrifice to procure a son who might avenge his defeat; two children were then born to him from the midst of the altar, out of the sacrificial fire, viz. a son Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna, and a daughter Draupadī or Kṛṣṇā, after-wards wife of the Pāṇḍavas.) —वेदि-प्रतिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, erected on sacrificial ground. —वेदि-मेखला, f. the boundary cord of a sacrificial ground. —वेदि-वत्, ind. like the sacrificial altar. —वेदीश (°दि-ईश), अस्, m. ‘lord of the Vedi,’ epithet of Agni; of Brahmā (as husband of Sarasvatī). —वेद्य्-अन्त, अस्, m. the end of the Vedi.
वेदिका: वेदिका, f. ground prepared for sacrificial cere-monies, a kind of altar; a quadrangular open shed in the middle of a court-yard (erected for various purposes and furnished with a seat, = वि-तर्दि); an arbour; a seat.
वेदित: वेदित, अस्, आ, अम्, make known, represented.
वेदितव्य: वेदितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be known or ascertained; to be made known, to be explained or expounded.
वेदितृ: वेदितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, knowing; a knower, &c.; wise, learned.
वेदिन्: वेदिन्, ई, इनी, इ, knowing, acquainted with; es-pousing, marrying (e. g. शूद्रा-वेदी, a man who marries a Śūdra woman); (ई), m. a knower; a teacher; a learned Brāhman; Brahmā; (इ), n. a kind of plant (= अम्ब-ष्ठा). —वेदि-ता, f. or वेदि-त्व, अम्, n. knowledge, wisdom, learning, experience.
वेदी: वेदी, f. = वेदि, an altar, &c. (See col. 2.)
वेदीयस्: वेदीयस्, आन्, असी, अस्, Ved. one who is wiser or very wise, (Sāy. = अतिशयेन विद्वस्, Ṛg-veda VII. 98, 1.)
वेद्य: 1. वेद्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be known or ascertained; to be made known; to be explained or taught; to be espoused or married; bringing or causing wealth (Ved., Sāy. = धन-हित, लाभ-हेतु).
2. वेद्य, अस्, आ, अम्, relating or agreeable to the Vedas.
वेदण्ड: वेदण्ड वेदण्ड, अस्, m. (a doubtful word), an elephant.
वेदमुख्या: वेदमुख्या वेदमुख्या, f. (a doubtful word, cf. वेध-मुख्य), a sort of insect, the winged bug.
वेदसिनी: वेदसिनी वेदसिनी, f., N. of a river, (also written वेद-वती, वेतसिनी।)
वेदार: वेदार वेदार, अस्, m. a chameleon; a lizard.
वेध: वेध वेध, अस्, m. (fr. rt. व्यध्), penetra-tion, piercing, breaking through, perforation; punc-turing, wounding, wound; hole, excavation; the depth of any excavation, depth (in measurement); a particular measure or division of time (= 100 Truṭis). —वेध-मुख्य, अस्, m. a kind of Curcuma, = कर्चूर; (आ), f. a kind of plant (= कस्तूरी). —वे-ध-मुख्यक, अस्, m. zedoary, Curcuma Zerum-bet (= हरिद्रा, द्राविडक).
वेद्धृ: वेद्धृ, धा, m. a piercer, perforator.
वेधक: वेधक, अस्, आ, or इका, अम्, piercing, perforating, a piercer or perforator (of gems); sharp; (अस्), m., N. of one of the divisions of Naraka; camphor; (अम्), n. grain, rice in the ear.
वेधन: वेधन, अम्, n. the act of piercing, perforation; penetration, excavation; puncturing, pricking; wound-ing; a thrust; depth (in measurement); (ई), f. an instrument for piercing an elephant's ear; a small gimblet (for perforating gems, shells, &c.); an auger, gimblet, piercing instrument (in general).
वेधनिका: वेधनिका, f. a sharp-pointed perforating instru-ment (used especially for piercing jewels or shells), an auger, awl, gimblet, &c.
वेधनीय: वेधनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, capable of being pierced, penetrable, vulnerable.
वेधित: वेधित, अस्, आ, अम्, pierced, perforated, pene-trated.
वेधिन्: वेधिन्, ई, इनी, इ, piercing, stabbing, perforating; hitting (a mark); (इनी), f. a leech. —वेधि-त्व, अम्, n. capacity of piercing.
वेध्य: वेध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be pierced or perforated; (अम्), n. a mark for shooting at, butt, target.
वेधस्: वेधस् वेधस्, आस्, आस्, अस् (according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 224. fr. वेध् substituted for वि-धा), arranging, creating; wise, learned (= मेधाविन्, Naigh. III. 15); (आस्), m. an arranger, disposer, creator, (कु-वेधस्, आस्, m. ‘evil creator,’ evil des-tiny); N. of Brahmā; of Viṣṇu; of Śiva; of the Sun; of Soma; a wise or learned man; a priest; a poet, Vedic Ṛṣi. —वेधस्-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. most wise, wisest, (Sāy. = अतिशयेन मेधाविन्।)
वेधस: वेधस, अम्, n. the part of the hand under the root of the thumb (considered as sacred to Brahmā, see तीर्थ); (अस्), m., N. of a Vedic Ṛṣi (said to belong to the family of Aṅgiras).
वेधस्या: वेधस्या, f., Ved. a desire of performing sacri-fices, (Sāy. = याग-विधानेच्छा।)
वेन्: वेन् वेन् (also written वेण्, q. v.), cl. 1. P. A. वेनति, -ते, विवेन, विवेने, वेनि-तुम्, to go, move; to move about, circulate (Ved., cf. वेनस्); to care for, be anxious for, wish, desire, love, favour (Ved.); to praise, worship (Ved.); to know, perceive, discern, recognise, reflect; to take; to play on an instrument: Caus. वेनयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अविवेनत्: Desid. विवेनिषति, -ते: Intens. वे-वेन्यते, वेवेन्ति; [cf. Gr. αἰνέω, αἴνη.]
वेन: वेन, अस्, m., Ved. a friend, lover, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VIII. 63, 1 = कान्त); a knower, discerner, wise man; = यज्ञ (Naigh. III. 17); a priest; N. of the Sun; of Prajā-pati or Brahmā; of a son of Aṅga, (also written वेण, q. v.); of the author of the hymns Ṛg-veda IX. 85, X. 123 (hav-ing the patronymic Bhārgava); (आ), f. a loved one; N. of the wife of Soma.
वेनत्: वेनत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. wishing, desiring, de-sirous; (अन्), m. a suppliant.
वेनस्: वेनस्, अस्, n., Ved. circulation (of the vital airs).
वेनि: वेनि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. loving, desiring, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VIII. 41, 3. वेनीः = कामय-मानाः प्रजाः।)
वेन्य: वेन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. to be loved or adored, adorable; (अस्), m., N. of a Vedic Ṛṣi; [cf. वैन्य।]
वेन्ना: वेन्ना वेन्ना, f. (according to Uṇādi-s. III. 8. fr. rt. वन्), N. of a river.
वेप्: वेप् वेप् (connected with the Caus. of rt. 1. वी), cl. 1. A. वेपते (ep. also P. वे-पति), विवेपे, वेपिष्यते, वेपितुम्, to tremble, shake, move about, quiver: Caus. वेपयति, -यितुम्, to cause to tremble or move; [cf. Lat. vibrare; Old Germ. weibon, weibjan.]
वेपथु: वेपथु, उस्, m. trembling, tremor. —वेपथु-परीत, अस्, आ, अम्, seized with or affected by tremor. —वेपथु-भृत्, त्, त्, त्, possessing tremor, trem-bling. —वेपथु-मत्, अन्, अती, अत्, possessed of tremor, trembling, quaking.
वेपन: वेपन, अम्, n. tremor, trembling; the discharg-ing of a bow, (in this sense perhaps to be connected with Caus. of rt. 1. वी।)
वेपमान: वेपमान, अस्, आ, अम्, trembling, shaking, quiver-ing, quaking.
वेपयत्: वेपयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, causing to tremble or quake, agitating; driving away, dispelling, (probably con-nected with Caus. of rt. 1. वी; according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VIII. 12, 2 = तमांसि वर्जयत्।)
वेपस्: वेपस्, अस्, n. trembling, tremor, (Sāy. = वेपन); act, activity, energy (enumerated among the कर्म-नामानि in Naigh. II. 1); = अनवद्य (according to Śabda-k.).
वेपी: वेपी, in Ṛg-veda VI. 22, 5. perhaps ‘accom-panied with ceremonial acts,’ (Sāy. = वेपस्, i. e. या-गादि-लक्षणं कर्म तद्-वती।)
वेर: वेर वेर, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. 1. वी), the body; the egg-plant (= वार्ताक); saffron.
वेरट: वेरट वेरट, अस्, m. a low man, one of a mixed or inferior caste; (अम्), n. the fruit of the jujube.
वेल्: वेल् 1. वेल् (rather to be regarded as a Nom. fr. वेला below), cl. 10. P. वेल-यति, -यितुम्, to count or declare the time.

वेल् 2. वेल् or वेल्ल् (also written वेह्ल्), cl. 1. P. वेलति or वेल्लति, &c., to go, move; to shake about, tremble, move about, move round; to be wanton; [cf. perhaps Gr. εἴλω, ελύω; Lat. volvo; Old Germ. wuoljan; Goth. valvjan; Angl. Sax. willian, wœltan.]
वेल: वेल, अम्, n. a garden, grove; (आ), f. time, season, (वेलायाम्, seasonably); opportunity, interval, leisure; tide, flow, stream, current; the coast, sea-shore, (वेलायाम्, on the sea-shore, coast-wise); boundary, limit; speech; passion, emotion, feeling; easy or painless death (= अक्लिष्ट-मरण); sickness, dis-ease, (according to Śabda-k. = राग-स्थाने रोगः); the gums; the food of Śiva (= ईश्वरस्य भोजनम्); N. of a daughter of Meru and wife of Samudra; of the wife of Budha. —वेलाकुल (°ला-आक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, agitated by the tide. —वेला-कूल, अम्, n. ‘stream-bank,’ N. of a district (the modern Tāmalipta or Tumlook, see ताम-लिप्त; said to be in the district of Midnapore or in the southern part of the present Hūglī district, forming the west bank of the Hūglī river at its union with the sea; a village called Beer-cool, said to be derived from Velā-kūla, is still found near the sea-shore). —वेला-मूल, अम्, n. the sea-shore. —वेला-वन, अम्, n. a wood on a shore or sea-coast. —वेलावली (°ला-आव्°), f., N. of a particular scale in Hindū music. —वेला-वित्त, अस्, m. (thought to be) a kind of judicial office.
वेल्ल: वेल्ल, अस्, m. going, moving; shaking; (अस्, अम्), m. n. a particular plant (the seed of which is used as a vermifuge (= विडङ्ग). —वेल्ल-ज, अम्, n. black pepper, Piper Nigrum.
वेल्लन: वेल्लन, अम्, n. going, shaking; rolling on the ground (as a horse &c.); a sort of rolling-pin with which cakes &c. are prepared; (ई), f. a species of Dūrvā grass (= माला-दूर्वा).
वेल्लन्तर: वेल्लन्तर, अस्, m. a particular tree (= वीर-तरु).
वेल्लहल: वेल्लहल, अस्, m. a libertine (= केलि-नागर).
वेल्लि: वेल्लि, इस्, f. a creeping plant; [cf. वल्लि।]
वेल्लिका: वेल्लिका or वेल्लिकाख्या (°का-आख्°), f. a plant (commonly called Bel Suṇṭh).
वेल्लित: वेल्लित, अस्, आ, अम्, shaken, trembling, tremulous; crooked; (अम्), n. going, moving; shaking.
वेलिभुक्प्रिय: वेलिभुक्प्रिय वेलिभुक्-प्रिय, अस्, m. a kind of fragrant mango.
वेविजान: वेविजान वेविजान, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Intens. of rt. 1. विज्), intimidating, terrifying, (Sāy. = भी-षयत्, Ṛg-veda IV. 26, 5.)
वेविदान: वेविदान वेविदान, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Intens. of rt. 1. विद्), Ved. knowing or finding out most effectually; obtaining very much.
वेविषत्: वेविषत् वेविषत्, अत्, अती, अत् (fr. rt. 2. विष्), Ved. engaged in sacred rites, (Sāy. वेविषतः = कर्माणि प्राप्नुवन्तः, Ṛg-veda VI. 21, 5.)
वेविषाण: वेविषाण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. contending with, (Sāy. = युद्धार्थं सङ्गत, Ṛg-veda VII. 18, 15.)
वेवी: वेवी वेवी (perhaps to be regarded as an Intens. of rt. 1. वी, q. v.), cl. 2. A. वेवीते (Ved. also P. वेवेति, 3rd pl. A. वेव्यते), &c., to go; to pervade, obtain; to conceive or become pregnant; to wish, desire, love; to throw, cast, hurl; to eat, consume.
वेश्: वेश् वेश्। See under rt. 1. वेस्, p. 967.
वेशक: वेशक, अस्, आ or इका, अम्, who or what enters, en-tering; (अस्), m. a house; (इका), f. entrance, ingress.
वेशन: वेशन, अम्, n. the act of entering; a house.
वेशन्त: वेशन्त, अस्, m. a basin, pool, small pond; a kind of ladle or basin for holding Soma (Ved., cf. वै-शन्त); fire.
वेशिन्: वेशिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a dress, dressed, assuming a particular dress or form; [cf. सर्व-व्°।]
वेश्मन्: वेश्मन्, अ, n. a house, dwelling, abode, mansion; a palace; N. of the fourth astrological house. —वेश्म-कर्मन्, अ, n. house-building. —वेश्म-कलिङ्ग, अस्, m. ‘house-kaliṅga,’ a kind of sparrow (= च-टक). —वेश्म-कूल, अस्, m. a kind of creeper (= चचेण्डा). —वेश्म-नकुल, अस्, m. the musk rat or shrew. —वेश्म-भू, ऊस्, f. building-ground, ground suitable for a house, the site of a habitation. —वेश्म-स्थूणा, f. the main post or column of a house.
वेश्य: वेश्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be entered, to be occupied, accessible; (अम्), n. a habitation, abode, (Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VI. 61, 14 = प्रवेशन); the habitation of harlots; (आ), f. a courtezan, harlot, prostitute, (sometimes written वेष्या); the plant Cissampelos Hexandra; a particular metre. —वेश्या-गण, अस्, m. a company of harlots. —वेश्या-गमन, अम्, n. going after prostitutes, debauchery. —वेश्या-गामिन्, ई, m. one who visits prostitutes, a whoremonger. —वेश्या-गृह, अम्, n. ‘harlot-house,’ a brothel. —वेश्याचार्य (°या-आच्°), अस्, m. the master or keeper of prostitutes or dancing girls, &c.; a pimp; a catamite. —वेश्या-जन, अस्, m. a courtezan. —वेश्या-जन-समाश्रय, अस्, m. a habitation of courtezans, brothel. —वेश्या-पण, अस्, m. reward or wages given to a harlot. —वेश्या-पति, इस्, m. the husband of a courtezan. —वेश्या-वार, अस्, m. a number or company of harlots. —वेश्याश्रय (°या-आश्°), अस्, m. a habitation of harlots, abode of courtezans.
वेशर: वेशर वेशर, अस्, m. (also written वेसर, q. v.), a mule.
वेश्वर: वेश्वर वेश्वर, अस्, m. See वेशर above.
वेशवार: वेशवार वेशवार, अस्, m. = वेसवार, a kind of condiment or seasoning.
वेशीजाता: वेशीजाता वेशीजाता, f. a kind of creeper (= पुत्र-दात्री).
वेष: वेष वेष, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 2. विष्), dress, ap-parel [cf. वेश]; ornament, decoration; (in Naigh. II. 1. वेषः, or according to another reading वेशः, is enumerated among the कर्म-नामानि।)
वेषण: वेषण, अस्, m. the shrub Cassia Sophora, = कास-मर्द; (आ), f. the plant Flacourtia Cataphracta, = वितुन्न; (अम्), n. occupation, possession, entrance.
वेष्य: वेष्य, अस्, m. water [cf. वेष्प]; (आ), f. a courtezan, harlot, (for वेश्या।)
वेष्य वेष्य। See under वेष, p. 966.
वेष्क: वेष्क वेषक, अस्, m. (perhaps fr. rt. 2. विष्), Ved. a noose for strangling a sacrificial victim.
वेष्ट्: वेष्ट् वेष्ट्, cl. 1. A. वेष्टते, विवेष्टे, वेष्टिष्यते, वेष्टितुम्, to surround, en-close, encompass, envelop, encircle, wind or twist round or about, wrap round; to dress: Caus. वेष्टयति, यितुम्, Aor. अविवेष्टत् and अववेष्टत्, to surround, encompass; to twist about; to invest, blockade: De-sid. विवेष्टिषते: Intens. वेवेष्ट्यते, वेवेष्टि।

वेष्टक: वेष्टक, अस्, आ, अम्, surrounding, encompassing; a surrounder; anything which encompasses or en-closes or invests; (अम्), n. a turban; a wrapper; exudation, resin, gum, &c.; turpentine; (अस्), m. an enclosure, wall, fence; a pumpkin-gourd.
वेष्टन: वेष्टन, अम्, n. the act of surrounding or en-compassing or enclosing or encircling, (अङ्गुलि-व्°, that which invests or encircles the fingers, a finger ring); grasping; anything that surrounds or encom-passes; an envelope, wrapper; an enclosure, fence, wall; a turban, garland, tiara, diadem; a girdle; a bandage, band; a covering, case; the outer ear (i. e. the meatus auditorius and concha); a particular attitude in dancing, (either a disposition of the hands or crossing of the feet); bdellium. —वेष्टन-वेष्-टक, अस्, m. a particular attitude of the sexes in coitus.
वेष्टनक: वेष्टनक, अस्, m. a particular position in coitus.
वेष्टनीय: वेष्टनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be surrounded or en-closed, to be wrapped or wound round.
वेष्टयत्: वेष्टयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, surrounding, encompassing.
वेष्टयित्वा: वेष्टयित्वा, ind. having bound round, having encompassed.
वेष्टित: वेष्टित, अस्, आ, अम्, surrounded, encompassed, enclosed, encircled, enveloped, bound or wound round, wrapped up; dressed; invested; impeded, stopped, blocked, secured from access; (अम्), n. en-compassing, encircling; one of the gestures or atti-tudes of dancing, (a particular motion of the fingers or a crossing of the feet.)
वेष्टितव्य: वेष्टितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be surrounded or encompassed, &c.
वेष्ट्य: वेष्ट्य, अस्, आ, अम्, = वेष्टितव्य above.
वेष्प: वेष्प वेष्प, अस्, m. water; [cf. वाष्प।]
वेस्: वेस् 1. वेस्, cl. 1. P. वेसति, वेसितुम्, to go, move; to desire, love, (Naigh. II. 6; another reading has वेशति।)

वेसर: वेसर वेसर, अस्, m. a mule, (also written वेशर।)
वेसवार: वेसवार वेसवार, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. विस्), a particular condiment or kind of seasoning (con-sisting of ground coriander, mustard, pepper, ginger, spice, &c.; also written वेशवार, वेषवार).
वेह्: वेह् वेह् (also written बेह्), cl. 1. A. वे-हते, विवेहे, वेहितुम्, to strive, make effort, endeavour diligently, resolve; cl. 1. P. वे-हति, &c. = वेहायते (according to Vopa-deva).
वेहत्: वेहत् वेहत्, त्, f. (said to be connected with वि-हन्), a cow miscarrying from taking the bull un-seasonably, a barren cow.
वेहाय: वेहाय, Nom. A. वेहायते, -यितुम्, to miscarry (as a cow).
वेहार: वेहार वेहार, अस्, m., N. of a country (Behār).
वेह्ल्: वेह्ल् वेह्ल्, cl. 1. P. वेह्लति, &c. = rt. वेल्, q. v.

वै 2. वै, ind. a particle of affirmation, generally translatable by ‘indeed,’ ‘truly,’ ‘certainly,’ ‘verily,’ ‘in sooth;’ it may also mean ‘so,’ ‘just,’ ‘although,’ ‘granted,’ ‘if,’ (तु वै, ‘but just;’ न वै, ‘perhaps not’); it is also said to be a vocative particle, and is often merely an expletive used for filling out a verse.
वैंशतिक: वैंशतिक वैंशतिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. विंशति), purchased with twenty.
वैकक्ष: वैकक्ष वैकक्ष, अम्, n. (fr. वि-कक्ष), a garland or string of flowers &c. worn over one shoulder and under the other (like the sacrificial thread); an upper garment, wrapper, mantle.

वैकङ्क: वैकङ्क वैकङ्क, N. of a mythical moun-tain.
वैकङ्कत: वैकङ्कत वैकङ्कत, अस्, m. (fr. वि-कङ्कत), the plant Flacourtia Sapida (= वृन्तिङ्कर).
वैकटिक: वैकटिक वैकटिक, अस्, m. (fr. वेकट), a jeweller.

वैकर्त: वैकर्त वैकर्त, अस्, m. (fr. वि-कर्त), Ved. one who cuts up a sacrificial victim, a butcher; a particular part of a slaughtered animal (cut off and given to the priests at a sacrifice).

वैकल्पिक: वैकल्पिक, अस्, ई, अम्, doubtful, dubious, uncer-tain, admitting of difference of opinion, indetermi-nate, alternative, optional (= वि-कल्पित).
वैकल्य: वैकल्य वैकल्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-कल), im-perfection, incompleteness, impairedness, deficiency, defect, mutilation, a defective or imperfect state of any limb or organ, lameness; incompetency, insuf-ficiency; agitation, flurry; non-existence.

वैकाल: वैकाल वैकाल, अस्, m. (fr. वि-काल), even-ing, afternoon, (वैकाले, loc. c. in the evening.)

वैकुण्ठ: वैकुण्ठ वैकुण्ठ, अस्, m. वैकृत: वैकृत वैकृत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-कृति), un-dergoing change, changed (in mind or form); modi-fied; (अम्), n. change, modification, alteration; change of mind, aversion, disgust. —वैकृत-सर्ग, अस्, m. a kind or form of creation, (opposed to प्रा-कृत-सर्ग।) —वैकृतापह (°त-अप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, removing or preventing change.

वैकृत्य: वैकृत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, changed (in form or mind); (अम्), n. change, alteration; aversion, disgust.
वैक्रान्त: वैक्रान्त वैक्रान्त, अम्, n. (fr. वि-क्रान्त), a kind of gem (= गो-नास, said to resemble a diamond or burnt diamond; according to others, the common loadstone or magnet).
वैक्लव: वैक्लव वैक्लव, अम्, n. (fr. वि-क्लव), agi-tation or distress of mind, bewilderment.

वैखान: वैखान वैखान, अस्, m., N. of Viṣṇu.
वैखानस: वैखानस वैखानस, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-खा-नस), instituted by hermits, relating to hermits, monastic; (अस्), m. a Brāhman of the third religious order, a Vānaprastha or hermit, anchorite; N. of a sect of Vaiṣṇavas, (in Taittirīya-ār. 1. 23, 3. the Vaikhānasas are represented as having sprung from the nails of Prajā-pati); a patronymic of the Vedic Ṛṣi Vamra, (Śataṃ Vaikhānasāḥ are regarded as the authors of the hymn Ṛg-veda IX. 66); (ई), f. a vessel used for frying the meal offered in sacrifice. —वैखानस-मत, अम्, n. the laws ordained for hermits, (according to Kullūka = वैखानस-शास्-त्रोक्तो धर्मः।)
वैगुण्य: वैगुण्य वैगुण्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-गुण), ab-sence of or freedom from qualities, absence of attri-butes; difference of qualities or properties, contra-riety of properties, diversity, contrariety; inferiority, baseness, badness, vileness; unskilfulness, awkward-ness, clumsiness, waywardness; fault, defect.
वैग्रहिक: वैग्रहिक वैग्रहिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-ग्रह), corporeal, bodily.

वैचित्त्य: वैचित्त्य वैचित्त्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-चित्ति), con-fusion of thought, distraction of mind, grief.

वैच्युत: वैच्युत वैच्युत, अस्, m. (fr. वि-च्युत), N. of a Muni.
वैजन: वैजन वैजन, अस्, m., N. of the author of the grammatical work called Prabodha-candrikā.
वैजनन: वैजनन वैजनन, अम्, n. (fr. वि-जनन), the last month of pregnancy (= प्रसव-मास).
वैजयन्त: वैजयन्त वैजयन्त, अस्, m. (fr. वि-जयन्त), the banner or emblem of Indra; a banner, flag; the palace of Indra; (ई), f. a flag, banner; an ensign; a kind of garland; the necklace of Viṣṇu (com-posed of five gems, viz. pearl, ruby, emerald, sap-phire, and diamond); N. of the eighth night of the civil month; the plant Sesbana Ægyptiaca; Premna Spinosa; N. of a lexicon.
वैजयन्तिक: वैजयन्तिक, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, bearing a flag; (अस्), m. a flag-bearer, standard-bearer; (आ), f. a flag, banner; a kind of scarf or a string or necklace of pearls; the plant Sesbana Ægyptiaca (= जयन्ती); another plant (= अग्नि-मन्थ).
वैजयि: वैजयि वैजयि, इस्, m. (fr. वि-जया), the third Jaina Cakra-vartin or emperor (= मघवन्).
वैजयिक: वैजयिक वैजयिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-जय), relating to victory, victorious.
वैजवाप: वैजवाप वैजवाप, अस्, m. (fr. वीज-वाप), N. of a Muni; of the author of a law-book.
वैजवापि: वैजवापि, इस्, इस्, इ (fr. वीज-वापिन्), see Gaṇa Sutaṅgamādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80; (इस्), m. a patro-nymic from Vīja-vāpa or Vīja-vāpin; (अयस्), m. pl., N. of a warrior-tribe.
वैजवापीय: वैजवापीय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वैजवापि), see Gaṇa Raivatikādi to Pāṇ. IV. 3, 131; (अस्), m. a prince of the Vaijavāpis.
वैजात्य: वैजात्य वैजात्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-जाति), differ-ence of class or species or kind, difference of caste, diversity of ordinary character or conduct, extraor-dinariness, strangeness; exclusion from caste; loose-ness, wantonness.
वैजिक: वैजिक वैजिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वीज), seminal, relating to seed, belonging to any primary cause or source or principle, original; relating to conception; relating to sexual union; (अस्), m. a young shoot, sprout, scion; (अम्), n. cause, source, origin, motive; the spiritual cause of existence, soul, spirit; oil pre-pared from the Śigru or Morunga.
वैजि: वैजि, इस्, इस्, इ, see Gaṇa Gahādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 138.
वैजीय: वैजीय, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. वैजि), see Gaṇa Gahādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 138.
वैजेय: वैजेय, अस्, m. a patronymic from Vīja.
वैज्ञानिक: वैज्ञानिक वैज्ञानिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-ज्ञान), conversant with, skilful, clever, proficient.
वैडाल: वैडाल वैडाल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. विडाल), of or belonging to a cat, peculiar to cats, feline. —वैडाल-व्रत, अम्, n. ‘cat-like observance,’ putting on a show of virtue or piety to conceal malice and evil designs. —वैडाल-व्रति, इस्, m. one who leads a chaste or continent life merely from the absence of women or temptation. —वैडालव्रतिक, अस्, ई, अम्, or वैडालव्रतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, acting like a cat, hypo-critical; any hypocritical religious impostor or pre-tended ascetic who, under an appearance of piety and virtue, conceals covetous or malignant designs (= भण्ड-तपस्विन्).
वैण: वैण वैण, अस्, m. (fr. वेणु), a cutter of bamboos, a maker of bamboo-work; N. of a Ṛṣi.
वैणव: वैणव, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to a bamboo, produced from or made of bamboo; (अस्), m. a student's staff cut from a bamboo, any bamboo staff; a worker in bamboo or wicker-work; N. of a sacred place of pilgrimage; (ई), f. bamboo manna; (अम्), n. the fruit or seed of the bamboo.
वैणविक: वैणविक, अस्, m. a flutist, piper, flute-player.
वैणविन्: वैणविन्, ई, m. epithet of Śiva.
वैणहोत्र: वैणहोत्र, अस्, m., N. of a king.

वैणुकेय: वैणुकेय, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or belonging to a bamboo, &c.
वैणिक: वैणिक वैणिक, अस्, m. (fr. वीणा), a lutanist, a player on the Vīṇā or Indian lute.

वैतण्ड्य: वैतण्ड्य, अस्, m., N. of a son of the Vasu Āpa.
वैतथ्य: वैतथ्य वैतथ्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-तथ), falseness.
वैतथ्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-तथ), falsehood, un-truth, untruthfulness.
वैतनिक: वैतनिक वैतनिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वेतन), living on wages, subsisting on a stipend; (अस्), m. a hireling, stipendiary; a labourer.
वैतरण: वैतरण वैतरण, अस्, m. (fr. वि-तरण), N. of a physician.

वैतस: वैतस वैतस, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वेतस), reed-like; (अस्), m. a sort of cane, Calamus Fasciculatus; = शेप (according to Naigh. III. 29).
वैतहव्य: वैतहव्य वैतहव्य, अस्, m. (fr. वीत-हव्य), a patronymic of the Vedic Ṛṣi Aruṇa.
वैतान: वैतान वैतान, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-तान), taken from the sacred hearth, sacrificial, sacred (as fire); (अम्), n. an oblation with fire; a sacrificial rite. —वैतान-कुशल, अस्, आ, अम्, skilled in or con-versant with sacrificial rites. —वैतानोपासना (°न-उप्°), f. the regular presentation of burnt-offerings morning and evening.

(fr. वीर), heroism, valour, prowess; enmity, hostility, animosity, revenge, grudge, malice, spite, hatred, vindictiveness, opposition, strife, quarrel. —वैर-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, causing hostility, occasioning enmity, mischief-making. —वैर-कार, अस्, m. ‘enmity-causer,’ an enemy. —वैर-कारण, अम्, n. a cause of hostility. —वैर-कृत्, त्, m. ‘causing enmity,’ an enemy. —वैर-निर्यातन, अम्, n. requital of enmity or of a grudge, revenge, retaliation, requital of an injury. —वैर-प्रति-क्रिया, f. requital of hostile acts, revenge. —वैर-प्रतिमोचन, अम्, n. deliverance or setting free from enmity. —वैर-प्रतियातन, अम्, n. the requital of enmity, taking vengeance. —वैर-यातना, f. requital of a grudge, vengeance. —वैर-रक्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, guarding against or warding off hos-tility. —वैर-शुद्धि, इस्, f. the removal or wiping out of a grudge, revenge, retaliation. —वैरातङ्क (°र-आत्°), अस्, m. the Arjuna tree. —वैरानुबन्-ध (°र-अन्°), अस्, m. beginning or commencement of hostilities. —वैरानुबन्धिन्, ई, इनी, इ, com-mencing hostilities, leading to or resulting in enmity or hostility; (ई), m. the calorific or heating solar ray; epithet of Viṣṇu. —वैरारोह (°र-आर्°), अस्, m. rise or advance of hostility, desperate combat. —वैरी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become hostile, be changed into enmity or hatred. —वै-रोद्धार (°र-उद्°), अम्, n. removal or redemption of a grudge, taking revenge, retaliation.
वैराय: वैराय, Nom. A. वैरायते, -यितुम्, to become hostile, behave inimically, act in a hostile manner, fight.
वैरायमाण: वैरायमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, becoming hostile or inimical, being an enemy.
वैरिन्: वैरिन्, ई, इणी, इ, hostile, malicious, revengeful; (ई), m. a hero; an enemy. —वैरि-ता, f. or वैरि-त्व, अम्, n. heroism; enmity, hostility, malice, hatred.
वैरक्त: वैरक्त वैरक्त, अम्, n. (fr. वि-रक्त), free-dom from worldly affections and passions, absence of affection or attachment, aversion, displeasure, dislike.
वैरङ्गिक: वैरङ्गिक वैरङ्गिक, अस्, m. (fr. वि-रङ्ग), one who has subdued all passions and desires, a devotee, ascetic.
वैरल्य: वैरल्य वैरल्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-रल), loose-ness or openness (of texture), fineness; rareness, scarceness.
वैराग: वैराग वैराग, अम्, n. (fr. वि-राग), absence of worldly passion, freedom from all desires.
वैरागिक: वैरागिक, अस्, m. an ascetic who has subdued his passions and is free from desire.
वैरागिन्: वैरागिन्, ई, m. an ascetic or devotee who has subdued all worldly desires; a particular class of reli-gious mendicants.
वैराग्य: वैराग्य, अम्, n. freedom from passion, dispas-sion, absence of all worldly desires and appetites, asceticism, devotion. —वैराग्य-शतक, अम्, n., N. of one hundred verses on asceticism by Bhartṛ-hari, (these verses constitute the third Śataka in his work.)
वैराज: वैराज वैराज, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 2. वि-राज्), consisting of the Virāj metre, composed in this metre; consisting of ten syllables (as a Pāda); of or belonging to the district called Virāj; epithet of particular worlds; (अस्), m. a son or descendant of Virāj, Manu Svāyambhuva; a patronymic of the Vedic Ṛṣi Ṛṣabha; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a parti-cular class of deities; of a class of Pitṛs; (अम्), n., N. of the Virāj metre; of a particular Sāman or portion of the Sāma-veda.
वैराजक: वैराजक, अस्, m. epithet of the nineteenth Kalpa.
वैराट: वैराट वैराट, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-राट), relat-ing or belonging to Virāṭa; (अस्), m. an earth-worm; a particular insect (= इन्द्र-गोप). —वैराट-देश, अस्, m., N. of a country. —वैराट-राज, अस्, m., N. of a king.
वैराट्या: वैराट्या, f., N. of one of the sixteen Vidyā-devīs or goddesses of learning (with Jainas).
वैरिण: वैरिण वैरिण, अस्, m. (see वीरण), Ved. a kind of Vīraṇa grass, (Sāy. = वीरण-प्रकार, Ṛg-veda 1. 191, 3.)
वैरूप: वैरूप वैरूप, अम्, n. (fr. वि-रूप), Ved., N. of a particular Sāman; (अस्), m. a patronymic of the Vedic Ṛṣi Aṣṭā-daṃṣṭra; of Nabha-pra-bhedana; of Śata-prabhedana; of Sadhri; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a race of Pitṛs (occupying the third or highest heaven).
वैरूप्य: वैरूप्य, अम्, n. difference or diversity of form, variety of shape; deformity, ugliness. —वैरूप्य-ता, f. deformity, malformation.
वैरोचन: वैरोचन वैरोचन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-रोचन), belonging to or coming from the Sun; descended from Virocana, &c.; (अस्), m. a Buddha (the third of the Dhyāni-buddhas); a patronymic of the cele-brated Daitya Bali (sovereign of Mahābali-pura, see बलि); of the son of Agni; of the son of Sūrya (the Sun); a Siddha, a sort of demigod or deified mortal. —वैरोचन-निकेतन, अम्, n. ‘abode of Bali,’ Pātāla or that portion of the lower regions over which Bali presides, (see बलि।)
वैरोचनि: वैरोचनि, इस्, m. a Buddha; a patronymic of Bali, (see above); of the son of Agni; of the son of Sūrya.
वैरोचि: वैरोचि वैरोचि, इस्, m., N. of the Daitya Vāṇa.
वैल: वैल वैल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. विल), relating or belonging to a hole or pit. —वैल-स्थ, अम्, n., Ved. a pit, burying-place, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda 1. 133, 3. महा-वैलस्थे = सर्वैर् गन्तव्ये महा-श्मशाने or नाग-लोके।) —वैल-स्थान, अम्, n., Ved. a place like a hole, a pit; a burying-place. —वैल-स्थानक, अम्, n., Ved. a pit.
वैलक्षण्य: वैलक्षण्य वैलक्षण्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-लक्षण), contrariety, difference, disparity, oppo-sition; पूर्वोक्त-वैलक्षण्येन, in opposition to what was before stated.
वैलक्ष्य: वैलक्ष्य वैलक्ष्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-लक्ष), absence of mark or characteristic; contrariety, re-verse, inversion; the reverse of what is usual or natural, unnaturalness, affectation; स-वैलक्ष्यम्, affectedly, in a forced manner, unnaturally.
वैलोम्य: वैलोम्य वैलोम्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-लोम), contrariety, reverseness, opposition, oppositeness.
वैल्व: वैल्व वैल्व, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. विल्व), relating or belonging to the Vilva tree; made of Vilva wood; (अम्), n. the fruit of the Vilva or Ægle Marmelos. —वैल्व-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made or con-sisting of the Vilva or of its wood, &c.
वैवधिक: वैवधिक वैवधिक, अस्, m. (fr. वि-वध), a dealer, peddler, hawker, vender of various sub-stances (as grain, oil, ghee, fruit, sweetmeats, &c., = विवधिक).
वैवर्ण्य: वैवर्ण्य वैवर्ण्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-वर्ण), diversity of colour, change of colour or complexion; deviation or secession from tribe or caste, &c.; hete-rogeneousness, diversity, difference.
वैवर्त: वैवर्त वैवर्त, अम्, n. (fr. वि-वर्त), revo-lution, change or modification of existence; [cf. ब्रह्म-वैवर्त।]
वैवस्वत: वैवस्वत वैवस्वत, अस्, m. (a patronymic fr. विवस्वत्), N. of Yama as son of Vivasvat, (see Yama); the seventh Manu or Manu of the present period (as son of Vivasvat and brother of Yama); the planet Saturn; one of the Rudras; (अम्), n., scil. अन्तर, epithet of the seventh or present Manv-antara (as presided over by Manu Vaivasvata); (ई), f. a patronymic of Yamī; the south, the southern quarter. —वैवस्वत-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a cele-brated shrine and Tīrtha. —वैवस्वत-मन्वन्-तर, अम्, n., N. of the seventh or present Manv-antara, q. v.
वैवाहिक: वैवाहिक वैवाहिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-वाह), belonging or relating to marriage, matrimonial, nup-tial; (अस्, अम्), m. n. a marriage, wedding; (अस्), m. a son's father-in-law or a daughter's father-in-law, i. e. the father of a son's wife or of a daughter's husband.
वैवाह्य: वैवाह्य, अस्, -ही, अम्, relating to marriage.
वैवृत्त: वैवृत्त वैवृत्त, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-वृत्ति), of or belonging to Vi-vṛtti; (अस्), m. a particular modi-fication of Vedic accent.
वैशद्य: वैशद्य वैशद्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-शद), white-ness; cleanness, purity, clearness, perspicuity.
वैशन्त: वैशन्त वैशन्त, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वेशन्त), Ved. belonging to the Soma ladle or cup; (अम्), n. a cup of Soma juice, (according to modern scholars Vaiśanta in Ṛg-veda VII. 33, 2. is probably the name of a river.)
वैशम्पायन: वैशम्पायन वैशम्पायन, अस्, m., N. of a celebrated sage (the original teacher of the Taittirīya-saṃhitā or collection of hymns of the Black Yajur-veda, see तैत्तिरीय-संहिता; he was also the nar-rator of the Mahā-bhārata to Janam-ejaya); N. of the author of a law-book.
वैशम्पायनीय: वैशम्पायनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, of or belonging to Vaiśampāyana.
वैशली: वैशली वैशली, f. [cf. विशला], N. of a town to the north of Pāṭali-putra; [cf. वैशाली।]
वैशस: वैशस वैशस, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. a form वि-शस, derived fr. वि-शस्; cf. वि-शसन), relating to slaughter or destruction, destructive; (अम्), n. rending in pieces; slaughter, destruction; distress, pain, anguish, hindrance, impediment.
वैशस्त्र: वैशस्त्र 1. वैशस्त्र, अम्, n. (fr. वि-शस्तृ), government, sway, rule.
2. वैशस्त्र, अम्, n. (fr. वि-शस्त्र), the state of being unarmed, defencelessness.
वैशाख: वैशाख वैशाख, अस्, m. (fr. वि-शाखा), the first of the twelve months constituting the Hindū solar year (answering to April-May); a churning-stick; (अम्), n. a particular attitude in shooting (standing with the feet a span apart); (ई), f. the day of full moon in the month Vaiśākha (= रक्त-पु-नर्नवा); N. of a wife of Vasu-deva. —वैशाख-वदि, ind. in the dark half of the month Vaiśākha.
वैशाख्य: वैशाख्य, अस्, m., N. of a Muni.
वैशारद्य: वैशारद्य वैशारद्य, अम्, n. (fr. विशारद), cleverness, expertness, skill.
वैशाल: वैशाल वैशाल, अस्, m. (fr. विशाल), N. of a Muni; (ई), f., N. of a town [cf. विशाला]; of a wife of Vasu-deva.
वैशिक: वैशिक वैशिक, अस्, m. (fr. वेश्या), a parti-cular kind of Nāyaka or lover (in erotic poetry), one who associates with courtezans; (अम्), n. harlotry, the allurements of harlots, arts of courtezans.
वैशिष्ट: वैशिष्ट वैशिष्ट, अम्, n. (fr. वि-शिष्ट), dis-tinction, difference (= वैशिष्ट्य below).
वैशिष्ट्य: वैशिष्ट्य, अम्, n. endowment with some dis-tinguishing property or attribute, endowment with, possession of; distinction, peculiarity, difference, the state of distinguishing or being distinguished, differ-encing; excellence.
वैशेषिक: वैशेषिक वैशेषिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. विशेष), characteristic; belonging to the Vaiśeṣika doctrine, (in this sense fr. वैशेषिक, अम्, n.); (अस्), m. a follower of the Vaiśeṣika doctrine; (अम्), n., N. of one of the two great divisions of the Nyāya school of philosophy founded by Kaṇāda, (it was probably a later development of the other great division or ‘Nyāya proper’ founded by Gau-tama, with which it agrees in its analytical method of treating the various subjects of inquiry, but from which it differs in propounding only seven categories or topics instead of sixteen; and more especially in its doctrine of विशेष, ‘particularity or individual essence,’ i. e. in its maintaining the eternally distinct or sui generis nature of the nine substances, air, fire, water, earth, mind, ether, time, space, and soul, of which the first five, including mind, are held to be atomic: the seven Padārthas or categories are, 1. Dravya, ‘substance,’ divided into nine, as above stated; 2. Guṇa, ‘quality,’ of which there are twenty-four [see गुण]; 3. Karman, ‘action;’ 4. Sāmānya, ‘genus’ and ‘species;’ 5. Viśeṣa, ‘particularity,’ described above; 6. Samavāya, ‘co-inherence’ or ‘perpetual intimate connection;’ 7. A-bhāva, ‘non-existence’ or ‘privation:’ Kaṇāda's system allows only two of the Pramāṇas, i. e. instruments or means of obtaining true knowledge, of the four admitted by the Nyāya proper, viz. प्रत्यक्ष or knowledge arising from contact of a sense with its object, and अनुमान, inference of three kinds [a priori, a pos-teriori, and analogy], but the other Pramāṇas are said by some to be contained in these two; the system is taught in the form of Sūtras, and the Vaiśeṣika-sūtras, like those of the Nyāya proper, have been commented on by a triple set of com-mentaries, and expounded in various works, of which the best known are the Bhāṣā-pariccheda with its commentary, called Siddhānta-muktāvalī, and the Tarka-saṅgraha.) —वैशेषिक-सूत्र, अम्, n. the aphorisms of the Vaiśeṣika branch of the Nyāya philosophy (attributed to Kaṇāda).
वैशेष्य: वैशेष्य, अम्, n. specific or generic distinction; difference, superiority, pre-eminence.
वैश्य: वैश्य वैश्य, अस्, m. (fr. 2. विश्), ‘a man who occupies the soil,’ ‘a man of the people,’ a Vaiśya or man of the third caste whose business was agriculture and trade; (आ), f. a woman of the Vaiśya caste. —वैश्य-कन्या, f. a Vaiśya damsel, girl of the agricultural class. —वैश्य-कर्मन्, अ, n. or वैश्य-क्रिया, f. the business of a Vaiśya, agriculture, trade. —वैश्य-ता, f. the state or condition of a Vaiśya, (वैश्यतां गम्, to become a Vaiśya.) —वैश्य-वृत्ति, इस्, f. the mode of life or occupation of a Vaiśya, agriculture, trade. —वैश्या-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, born of a Vaiśya woman, the child of a Vaiśya mother. —वैश्या-पुत्र, अस्, m. the son of a Vaiśya mother.
वैश्रवण: वैश्रवण वैश्रवण, अस्, m. (fr. वि-श्रवस्), ‘son of Viśravas,’ epithet of Kuvera, the god of wealth; of Rāvaṇa (younger brother of Kuvera); N. of the fourteenth Muhūrta. —वैश्रवणानुज (°ण-अन्°), अस्, m. the younger brother of Kuvera, i. e. Rāvaṇa. —वैश्रवणालय (°ण-आल्°) or वैश्र-वणावास (°ण-आव्°), अस्, m. ‘abode of Kuvera,’ the Indian fig-tree (= वट). —वैश्रवणोदय (°ण-उद्°), अस्, m. ‘Kuvera's glory,’ the Indian fig-tree.
वैश्वदेव: वैश्वदेव वैश्वदेव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. विश्व-देव), belonging or dedicated to the Viśva-devas or Viśve-devāḥ, (वैश्वदेवो लोकः, the world of the Viśva-devas, Manu IV. 183); offered to the Viśva-devas; relating to all the divinities; (अम्), n. an offering or sacrifice to the Viśva-devas; an offering to all deities (said to be performed by casting a little food into fire before a meal); (ई), f. the eighth day of the second half of the month Māgha; a species of the Paṅkti metre. —वैश्वदेव-कर्मन्, अ, n. an oblation to the Viśva-devas; an offering to the deities collectively. —वैश्वदेव-होम, अम्, n. oblation to the Viśva-devas.
वैश्वानर: वैश्वानर वैश्वानर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. विश्वा-नर), relating to or fit for all men, present with all men, common to all mankind, benefiting all men; (अस्), m. ‘son of Viśvā-nara,’ epithet of Agni or Fire, (Agni Vaiśvānara is regarded as the author of the hymns Ṛg-veda X. 79, 80); the fire of digestion; N. of a Dānava; (in the Vedānta phil.) ‘the Spirit of Humanity,’ N. of Intellect located in the collective aggregate of bodies, the general consciousness; (ई), f. a particular sacrifice performed at the beginning of every year; a particular division of the sun's path.
वैश्वानरीय: वैश्वानरीय, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. relating to Vaiśvā-nara; (अम्), n., scil. सूक्त, a particular Vedic hymn.
वैश्वामित्र: वैश्वामित्र वैश्वामित्र, अस्, m. (fr. विश्वा-मित्र), a son or descendant of Viśvā-mitra, a patro-nymic of several Vedic Ṛṣis; (ई), f. a female descendant of Viśvā-mitra.
वैश्वासिक: वैश्वासिक वैश्वासिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-श्वास), deserving confidence, trustworthy.
वैश्वी: वैश्वी वैश्वी, f. (fr. विश्व), N. of the Nak-ṣatra called Uttarā Aṣāḍhā or Uttarāṣāḍhā (so called because the Viśva-devas preside over this asterism).
वैषम्य: वैषम्य वैषम्य, अम्, n. (fr. विषम), inequality, unevenness, oddness (opposed to evenness); difficulty; calamity, misery, distress; injustice, harsh-ness; solitariness, singleness.
वैषयिक: वैषयिक वैषयिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. विषय), relating to an object, having for an object, (the आधार of an action is called वैषयिक when it is the aim or object of the action); belonging or relating to an object of sense, sensual, carnal; (अस्), m. a sensualist, one addicted to the pleasures of sense, one occupied with worldly objects or interests.
वैषुवत: वैषुवत वैषुवत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. विषु-वत्), relating to the equinox, equinoctial.
वैष्टुत: वैष्टुत वैष्टुत, अम्, n. (fr. वि-ष्टुत), the ashes of a burnt-offering.
वैष्ट्र: वैष्ट्र वैष्ट्र, अम्, n. (in Uṇādi-s. IV. 159. fr. rt. 1. विश्), the world, a division of the universe, = पिष्टप; (अस्), m. (?), the sky (= 3. दिव्); air, wind (= वायु); N. of Viṣṇu (according to Śabda-k.).
वैष्णव: वैष्णव वैष्णव, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or be-longing to Viṣṇu; worshipping Viṣṇu; (अस्), m. ‘a worshipper or follower of Viṣṇu,’ N. of one of the three great divisions of modern Hindū sects, (the other two being the Śaivas and Śāktas; the Vaiṣṇavas believe in the supremacy of Viṣṇu over the other gods of the Tri-mūrti; they are divided into six principal sects, as follow, 1. the Rāmānujas or Śrī-sampradāyins, founded by the celebrated re-former Rāmānuja, who flourished in the south of India towards the latter part of the twelfth century; their chief authoritative works are the Vedānta-sūtras and other Vedānta works, the Pañca-rātra of Nārada, the Viṣṇu-Purāṇa and other Pu-rāṇas: 2. the Rāmānandas, a sect founded by Rāmā-nanda, disciple of Rāmānuja, and very numerous in Gangetic India; they worship Viṣṇu under the form of Rāma-candra and his consort Sītā; their favourite work is the Bhakta-mālā: 3. the followers of Kabīr, a celebrated disciple of Rāmānanda, principally found in upper and central India; they do not observe all the ceremonies of the Hindūs, but conform to the usages of caste, and pay a sort of respect to Viṣṇu: 4. the Vallabhācāryas or Rudra-sampradāyins, see वल्ल-भाचार्य; this sect draws its doctrines from the Bhāgavata-Purāṇa and works of Vallabha: 5. the Mādhvas or Brahma-sampradāyins, founded by Ma-dhvācārya, who is regarded by his followers as an incarnation of Vāyu, the god of wind;
